commands:
trusscli — TrussC project tool

Usage:
  trusscli <command> [options]
  trusscli                       Launch the GUI (TrussC Project Generator)

Commands:
  new <path>                     Create a new project at <path>
  cp <src> <dst>                 Copy an existing project to <dst>
  update                         Regenerate build files for the project in CWD
  upgrade                        Upgrade TrussC (git pull + rebuild trusscli)
  addon <command>                Manage addons: list, add, remove, clone, pull, search
  info [section]                 Show project / framework info
  doctor                         Check development environment
  clean                          Delete build directories
  build                          Build the project
  run                            Build and launch the project
  dist                           Package the project to run on another machine
  version                       Show version (trusscli + current TrussC)

Common options (per subcommand):
  -p, --path <path>              Operate on a specific project path
      --tc-root <path>           Path to TrussC root directory
  -h, --help                     Show command-specific help
  -v, --version                  Show version (trusscli + current TrussC)

Examples:
  trusscli new myApp                        Create ./myApp
  trusscli new ./apps/myApp --web           Create with Web build enabled
  trusscli new myApp -a tcxOsc -a tcxIME    With addons
  trusscli addon add tcxOsc                 Add an addon to existing project
  trusscli addon remove tcxOsc              Remove an addon
  trusscli addon clone tcxGPT               Download an addon from the registry
  trusscli update                           Regenerate the project in CWD
  trusscli update -p ./apps/myApp           Regenerate a specific project

Run 'trusscli <command> --help' for command-specific help.
commands.addon:
Usage: trusscli addon <command> [options]

Manage addons for TrussC projects.

Commands:
  list                       List addons (local + optionally remote)
  add <addon>...             Add addons to the project
  remove <addon>...          Remove addons from the project
  clone <addon>...           Clone addons from the registry
  pull [<addon>...] [--all]  Update addons via git pull
  search <query>             Search the addon registry

Run 'trusscli addon <command> --help' for command-specific help.
commands.addon add:
Usage: trusscli addon add <addon> [<addon>...]

Add one or more addons to the TrussC project in the current directory.
The project is detected by walking up from CWD. The addons.make file
is updated and the build files are regenerated.
The IDE and the Web / Android / iOS targets are kept from the
project's CMakePresets.json (change them with 'trusscli update').
A kept target that fails to configure is reported as a warning.

Options:
  -p, --path <path>          Operate on a specific project path
      --tc-root <path>       Path to TrussC root directory
  -h, --help                 Show this help

Examples:
  trusscli addon add tcxOsc                      Add a single addon
  trusscli addon add tcxOsc tcxImGui tcxBox2d    Add multiple addons at once
commands.addon clone:
Usage: trusscli addon clone <addon> [<addon>...]

Clone addon(s) from the registry into the TrussC addons/ folder.
Accepted addon forms:
  tcxFoo                 — registry lookup (asks if not found)
  owner/tcxFoo           — exact GitHub repo
  https://host/user/repo — direct HTTPS clone URL
  git@host:user/repo     — direct SSH clone URL

After cloning, dependencies declared in the addon's addon.json
are offered for installation (y/n).

Options:
      --no-interactive       Accept dep prompts, fail unknown names
      --tc-root <path>       TrussC root directory
  -h, --help                 Show this help
commands.addon list:
Usage: trusscli addon list [options]

List addons. By default shows locally available addons and which
are installed in the current project. Use --remote to also show
addons available from the registry.

Options:
      --remote               Include addons from the online registry
      --names                Output only names, one per line
                             (for shell completion; non-bundled
                             entries appear as bare 'name' and
                             'owner/name' for prefix matching)
      --cached               Prefer the on-disk registry cache;
                             avoids a network roundtrip
                             (used by shell completion)
  -p, --path <path>          Project path (for installed check)
      --tc-root <path>       TrussC root directory
  -h, --help                 Show this help
commands.addon pull:
Usage: trusscli addon pull [<addon>...] [--all]

Update addon(s) by running git pull in their directory.
Only affects addons that were cloned via git (have a .git/ folder).

Options:
      --all                  Pull all git-based addons
      --tc-root <path>       TrussC root directory
  -h, --help                 Show this help
commands.addon remove:
Usage: trusscli addon remove <addon> [<addon>...]

Remove one or more addons from the TrussC project in the current
directory. The project is detected by walking up from CWD. The
addons.make file is updated and the build files are regenerated.
The IDE and the Web / Android / iOS targets are kept from the
project's CMakePresets.json (change them with 'trusscli update').
A kept target that fails to configure is reported as a warning.

Options:
  -p, --path <path>          Operate on a specific project path
      --tc-root <path>       Path to TrussC root directory
  -h, --help                 Show this help

Examples:
  trusscli addon remove tcxOsc              Remove a single addon
  trusscli addon remove tcxOsc tcxImGui     Remove multiple addons at once
commands.addon search:
Usage: trusscli addon search <query>

Search the addon registry by name or description.
commands.build:
Usage: trusscli build [options]

Build the TrussC project in the current directory. By default builds
for the native platform; use --web / --android / --ios to cross-compile.

Options:
      --web                  Build for WebAssembly
      --android              Build for Android
      --ios                  Build for iOS
      --debug                Build type: Debug (-O0 -g)
      --relwithdebinfo       Build type: RelWithDebInfo (-O2 -g) [default]
      --release              Build type: Release (-O3, no debug info)
      --clean                Clean before building (--clean-first)
      --mcp                  Enable MCP development tools for this build
      --warnings             Enable -Wall -Wextra on your app's sources
  -j, --jobs <N>             Run at most N compile jobs at once
      --verbose              Show the full build output on screen
      --dry-run              Print the cmake commands instead of running them
  -p, --path <path>          Operate on a specific project path
  -h, --help                 Show this help

Output: the screen shows one progress line (a dot per 5 %), the warnings
and errors, and a short summary. The full output is always saved to
<build folder>/build.log (overwritten on each build). --verbose also shows
it on screen.

Without -j the build tool decides the job count (Linux limits it by
available RAM).

Build type applies to native builds; web/android keep their own
(MinSizeRel / Release). The three build-type flags are mutually exclusive.

When the target's build folder has no CMake cache (after 'trusscli clean',
or a deleted folder) or only the cache of a failed configure, build
configures it first. On Windows, when Visual Studio changed since the
project was generated (the MSVC, SDK or ninja path in CMakePresets.json
is gone), build detects Visual Studio again, replaces only those paths
in CMakePresets.json and removes build-windows before configuring.
It prints what it did.
commands.clean:
Usage: trusscli clean [options]

Delete build directories for the TrussC project in the current directory.
By default deletes the native platform build directory. Use --all to
delete all build directories (web, android, xcode-ios, etc.) and the
build scripts trusscli generated (build-web.sh / .command / .bat).

Options:
      --all                  Delete all build directories and generated build scripts
  -p, --path <path>          Operate on a specific project path
  -h, --help                 Show this help
commands.cp:
Usage: trusscli cp <src> <dst> [options]

Copy an existing TrussC project to a new location. If <src> is a
git work tree, only git-tracked and non-ignored files are copied
(so .gitignore controls what counts as generated). Otherwise a
built-in skip list for known build/IDE artifacts is used.
Generated build / IDE files are re-created at the destination.

Options:
  -n, --dry-run              Show what would be copied, don't modify anything
      --no-git               Force the built-in skip list even if <src> is a git repo
      --web                  Enable Web (WebAssembly) build
      --android              Enable Android build
      --ios                  Enable iOS build
      --ide <type>           IDE: vscode, cursor, xcode, vs, cmake (default: vscode)
      --tc-root <path>       Path to TrussC root directory (auto-detected by default)
  -h, --help                 Show this help

Examples:
  trusscli cp myApp myApp2               Duplicate ./myApp to ./myApp2
  trusscli cp . ../myApp2                Copy current project to sibling dir
  trusscli cp -n ../ref/myApp ./fork     Preview without copying
commands.dist:
Usage: trusscli dist [options]

Package the TrussC project in the current directory so it runs on another
machine: a self-contained folder in dist/, optionally archived.

Options:
      --release              Build as Release instead of RelWithDebInfo (no symbols)
      --archive, --zip       Also write a zip (Windows/macOS) or tar.gz (Linux)
      --installer            Also build an installer: <package>-setup.exe with NSIS
                             (Windows; 'winget install NSIS.NSIS'), or a package for
                             the Linux distribution it runs on (pacman on Arch and
                             derivatives, .deb on Debian/Ubuntu and derivatives)
      --no-build             Package the existing build (refuses a Debug build)
      --dry-run              List what would go into the package, change nothing
      --init                 Write a dist.json template (never overwrites) and stop
  -o, --output <dir>         Output folder (default: dist/ in the project)
      --app-name <name>      With --init: no question; otherwise overrides dist.json
      --app-version <x.y.z>  Same, for the version (a leading 'v' is dropped)
      --app-author <name>    Same, for the author
  -j, --jobs <N>             As in 'trusscli build'
      --verbose              As in 'trusscli build'
  -p, --path <path>          Operate on a specific project path
  -h, --help                 Show this help

The package is <name>-<version>-<platform>-<arch>/ with the executable, bin/data
(minus dist.json "exclude"), dist.json "include" entries, the VC++ runtime
DLLs the app imports (Windows), licenses/ and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt.
Windows .pdb symbols go to <name>-<version>-<platform>-<arch>-symbols/, beside it.
On macOS bin/data goes into the bundle's Contents/Resources/data and the bundle
is signed ad hoc.
On Linux <platform> is the distribution it was built on (arch, ubuntu24.04, ...):
the app uses that distribution's shared libraries and runs where they match.
A Linux package installs the app to /opt/<package>/ with a Start menu entry,
and the package manager installs the libraries it needs.

Settings come from dist.json in the project folder (optional; see --init):
name, version, author, eulaFile, include, exclude, licenses, and installer
(showEula, showNotices). Your license terms (eulaFile, or EULA.txt in the
project folder) go into the package as EULA.txt. The Windows installer asks
about shortcuts and starting at login.
trusscli collects the license files it finds; checking them is up to you.
More: docs/guides/DISTRIBUTION.md
commands.doctor:
Usage: trusscli doctor [options]

Check your development environment for TrussC build prerequisites.
By default shows only essential checks and any failures. Use --verbose
to see all checks including optional tools and cross-compile targets.
On Windows, inside a project, it also checks that the Visual Studio
paths pinned in CMakePresets.json (MSVC, Windows SDK, ninja) still
exist, and whether the last Ninja build recorded header dependencies
for main.cpp.obj.

Options:
      --verbose              Show all checks (including OK / optional / skipped)
      --json                 Machine-readable JSON output
  -p, --path <path>          Check against a specific project's target list
      --tc-root <path>       Path to TrussC root directory
  -h, --help                 Show this help
commands.info:
Usage: trusscli info [section] [options]

Show information about the TrussC project in the current directory.
If no project is found, prints framework info instead (TrussC root,
available addons).

Sections:
  (default)                  All sections
  project                    Project name, path, TrussC root
  targets                    Enabled build targets
  addons                     Addons listed in addons.make
  licenses                   License files 'trusscli dist' would collect (not in 'all')

Options:
  -p, --path <path>          Operate on a specific project path
      --tc-root <path>       Path to TrussC root directory
      --json                 Machine-readable JSON output
      --format <fmt>         Output format: human, plain, json (default: human)
  -h, --help                 Show this help

Examples:
  trusscli info                    Full human-readable overview
  trusscli info addons             Just the addon list
  trusscli info --json             Full info as JSON
  trusscli info addons --format plain   Grep-friendly addon list
commands.new:
Usage: trusscli new <path> [options]

Create a new TrussC project at <path>. The project name is the last
path component (e.g. `trusscli new ./apps/myApp` creates ./apps/myApp
with name 'myApp').
Project/binary names replace bytes outside ASCII letters, digits, _ . + -
with _; reserved names get app_. The folder keeps its name.

Options:
      --web                  Enable Web (WebAssembly) build
      --android              Enable Android build
      --ios                  Enable iOS build
      --ide <type>           IDE: vscode, cursor, xcode, vs, cmake (default: vscode)
  -a, --addon <name>         Add an addon. Repeatable, comma-list also OK
      --addons <list>        Same as -a, alternative spelling
      --tc-root <path>       Path to TrussC root directory (auto-detected by default)
  -h, --help                 Show this help
commands.run:
Usage: trusscli run [options]

Build and launch the TrussC project in the current directory.
Default: native build + launch. Use --web / --android / --ios to
cross-compile and launch on the appropriate target.

Options:
      --web                  Build WASM and start a local HTTP server
      --android              Build, adb install, and launch    [not yet implemented]
      --ios                  Build and run in iOS Simulator    [not yet implemented]
      --session <backend>    Launch inside a display session (Linux, no desktop).
                             Backends: labwc, x11. Example: --session labwc
      --debug                Build type: Debug (-O0 -g)
      --relwithdebinfo       Build type: RelWithDebInfo (-O2 -g) [default]
      --release              Build type: Release (-O3, no debug info)
      --mcp                  Enable MCP development tools for this build
      --warnings             Enable -Wall -Wextra on your app's sources
  -j, --jobs <N>             Run at most N compile jobs at once
      --verbose              Show the full build output on screen
  -p, --path <path>          Operate on a specific project path
  -h, --help                 Show this help

Only the build is shortened (see 'trusscli build --help'); the app's own
output is not filtered.
commands.update:
Usage: trusscli update [options]

Regenerate build files (CMakeLists.txt, CMakePresets.json, IDE files)
for the TrussC project in the current directory. The addon list is
read from the existing addons.make.
Project/binary names replace bytes outside ASCII letters, digits, _ . + -
with _; reserved names get app_. The folder keeps its name.

The IDE, the Web / Android / iOS targets and the web backend are kept
from the project's CMakePresets.json. Flags change them: --ide switches
the IDE, --web adds a target, --no-web drops it. Without a
CMakePresets.json (e.g. a fresh clone) the defaults apply: vscode,
native only.
A kept target is configured again. Its saved toolchain path is reused
when this shell has no emsdk / NDK set up; if its configure still
fails, that is a warning (fix the toolchain, or drop the target with
--no-web / --no-android / --no-ios). A target passed as a flag must
configure, or update fails.
A dropped target's build folder and build script stay in place;
'trusscli clean --all' removes them.

Options:
  -p, --path <path>          Operate on a specific project path
      --web                  Enable Web build
      --android              Enable Android build
      --ios                  Enable iOS build
      --no-web               Disable Web build
      --no-android           Disable Android build
      --no-ios               Disable iOS build
      --ide <type>           IDE: vscode, cursor, xcode, vs, cmake
      --tc-root <path>       Path to TrussC root directory
      --verbose              Show the full CMake configure output
  -h, --help                 Show this help

The CMake configure output is shortened on screen (its "-- ..." lines are
hidden; errors still show) and saved to <build folder>/build.log.
commands.upgrade:
Usage: trusscli upgrade [options]

Upgrade TrussC to the latest version by pulling the latest code from
the git repository and rebuilding trusscli. The /usr/local/bin symlink
(if present) automatically points to the new binary.

On Windows, tools/build_win.bat sets up Visual Studio and rebuilds
trusscli. The previous executable is removed on the next start.

Options:
      --tc-root <path>       Path to TrussC root directory
  -j, --jobs <N>             Run at most N compile jobs in the rebuild
  -h, --help                 Show this help
commands.version:
Usage: trusscli version

Show version (trusscli + current TrussC).

Options:
  -h, --help                 Show this help
